card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Former brand partnerships manager at a London luxury accessories label, made redundant in a restructure eight months ago. She describes herself as 'consulting' and is 'between roles'.
card.education_detail: Laurea triennale in Communication Sciences from the University of Turin, then an MA in Luxury Brand Management at a London university, which brought her to the UK at 23.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tom, 34, a British senior associate at a City law firm, in a rented two-bedroom flat in a converted Victorian house off the New King's Road. They married three years ago in a church near her parents' home in Piedmont. They have no children yet and talk about it a lot. The second bedroom is her 'office' and the guest room for her mother's visits.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Turin, northern Italy, to a dentist father and a mother who taught secondary school. She was brought up Catholic, still goes to Mass at Christmas and Easter, and sometimes goes to the Italian church in Clerkenwell when she feels homesick. She has been in London eight years, holds settled status and is thinking about British citizenship. She feels very Italian about food and family and fairly Londoner about everything else.
card.professional_persona: She is polished and good in a room. She is very aware of who matters, and she is good at making senior people feel flattered. At her last job she was known for landing influencer and hotel collaborations, and for taking a generous share of the credit. Her LinkedIn makes her sound slightly more senior than she was. She is anxious about the gap on her CV and covers it with talk of 'freelance strategy work' for a friend's candle brand.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty, but she keeps fit as part of the image. She goes to reformer Pilates twice a week at a boutique studio in Parsons Green and walks along the river at Bishop's Park. She watches Juventus matches with her dad over FaceTime, mostly to keep him company.
card.arts_persona: She loves design, fashion exhibitions and photography. She has a V&A membership and makes sure she gets to private views at the Saatchi and small Mayfair galleries. She reads Elena Ferrante in Italian and contemporary novels in English. She cries easily at films and refuses to watch anything with animals dying.
card.travel_persona: She goes back to Turin three or four times a year, and her mother visits in between. Holidays tend to be curated: Puglia, Lisbon, a boutique riad in Marrakech, a ski week in Courmayeur with Tom's university friends. She researches hotels obsessively and will happily pay for the upgrade. She gets very anxious about flights and connections.
card.culinary_persona: She cooks properly. She makes her nonna's agnolotti on Sundays and is snobbish about British 'Italian' food. She shops at the Italian deli on the Fulham Road and the market on North End Road. She loves trying the new restaurant everyone is talking about and likes being able to say she got a table. She calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: vintage designer handbag hunting on resale sites
restaurant openings in west and central London
styling the flat and flower arranging
skills: fluent Italian and English, decent French
brand partnerships and negotiating with agencies
social media content and styling for shoots
networking and making people feel important
spotting a fake handbag at ten paces
card.career_goals: She wants to get back into luxury, ideally a senior partnerships or brand director role at a fashion house or hotel group, because the title matters to her. She sometimes floats launching her own consultancy or a small Italian homeware brand, mostly because it would sound impressive. Privately she worries she has lost momentum and is scared of starting a family before she has 'made it'.
card.voice: She is fluent and quick, with a clear Italian accent. Her vowels are open, she sometimes stresses the wrong syllable, and her intonation goes up and down a lot. Eight years in London have given her plenty of 'sort of', 'to be honest' and 'literally', and the occasional 'yeah, no'. She hesitates with a soft 'erm', and sometimes the Italian 'eh' or 'cioè' slips out when she is searching for a word. She uses 'sorry' a lot, both to apologise and to correct herself mid-sentence: 'I was there for, sorry, five years.' She talks with her hands and gets animated and slightly breathless when she cares about something. Silence makes her nervous, so she fills it, often by asking 'Does that make sense?' or 'Is that what you mean?' She echoes the interviewer's phrasing back to them.
card.typing: Mostly correct sentence case and apostrophes, with the odd non-native slip, such as 'informations' or a missing article. She uses '...' a lot to trail off and sometimes an exclamation mark to sound friendly. Quick answers can drop the capital at the start. She rarely abbreviates beyond 'tbh' and 'etc'.
card.with_strangers: Warm, charming and quick to compliment. She asks about you, finds something in common and drops a well-placed detail about her husband's firm or a restaurant she has been to. She comes across as confident at first, but nerves show through if she feels judged. She overexplains, checks she has given the 'right' answer and may quietly shade the truth to look good.
small_things: the new Pilates instructor who is 'literally terrifying'
a restaurant in Soho she finally got a booking at
her mum's latest visit and the amount of food she brought in her suitcase
the British weather and how no one owns a proper coat

the deli that does real mortadella
deeper_things: how much the redundancy shook her and that she tells people she chose to take a break
worrying about fertility and feeling pressure from her family to have children
feeling she lives partly off Tom's salary, which makes her both grateful and resentful
guilt about her father's health and being a two-hour flight away
a fear that she is a bit superficial, which she rarely admits
loneliness in London despite a busy social calendar
lying awake anxious about money even though they are comfortable
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up, framing her from mid-chest up and a little left of centre. The light is soft daylight from a window to her right, which leaves the left side of her face in slight shadow. She has a light olive complexion, dark brown eyes, groomed eyebrows, minimal makeup and a nude lipstick. Her expression is a polite, slightly expectant smile. Her dark brown, shoulder-length hair is blow-dried with loose waves and tucked behind one ear. She has small gold hoop earrings and a thin gold chain with a tiny cross. She wears a cream fine-knit jumper and no glasses. Behind her is a white-painted wall with a framed black-and-white photograph of a Turin piazza, a narrow oak shelf holding a row of fashion and design coffee-table books, a scented candle and a small vase of white ranunculus. Part of a rattan chair and the edge of a grey linen curtain are visible on the right.
